in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know you're looking to claim for Alex, your 6-year-old son.

I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

Are you responsible for Alex? This means he either lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after him (at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

Next, could you tell me where you live? Specifically, are you currently living in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Are you or the other parent (if applicable) working and paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or are you receiving any UK benefits such as a pension or bereavement benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working in the UK or paying National Insurance there, and I'm not receiving any UK benefits either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just to cover all bases, is Alex's other parent (if there is one involved) either:
- Working in the UK and paying National Insurance contributions, or
- A Crown servant posted overseas (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex's other parent isn't working in the UK or paying National Insurance, and they're not a Crown servant either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:**

To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to either:
- Live in the UK, or
- Have a qualifying connection to the UK (such as working in the UK and paying National Insurance, being a Crown servant posted overseas, or receiving certain UK benefits)

Since you currently live abroad and neither you nor Alex's other parent has a qualifying connection to the UK (neither of you is working in the UK, paying UK National Insurance, receiving UK benefits, or serving as a Crown servant), you do not meet the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit at this time.

**If your circumstances change** – for example, if you return to live in the UK or begin working in the UK – you may become eligible in the future, and I'd encourage you to check again at that time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
